sections.h2: Which Gaston County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Gaston County splits the work between the Tax Office, which values property and takes appeals, and the Tax Collector, which bills and collects. The Tax Office is at 128 West Main Avenue, Gastonia, NC 28052, with a mailing address of P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053, and it is open Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 5 pm.

The main number is 704-866-3158. Extension 1 reaches the Tax Collector's Office, which sits at 100 East Garrison Boulevard in Gastonia, and extension 2 reaches the Real Estate Appraisal Department. Questions about relief programs go to option 6, and exemptions for religious, charitable and similar property go to option 2. Under North Carolina law the assessor lists, appraises and assesses real estate for the county, and the collector uses the remedies in the Machinery Act to collect what is billed.

sections.html:

sections.h2: When are Gaston County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills are due September 1, and the county says residents have until January 5 to pay without interest. Taxes become delinquent on January 6.

  • Interest of 2% starts on January 6.
  • After that, interest accrues at three-quarters of one percent per month until the balance is paid.
  • Delinquent accounts face levy, wage garnishment, attachment of rent or bank accounts, in rem foreclosure and mortgage style foreclosure.
  • Business personal property is listed during January.

The statewide listing period for real property opens on the first business day in January and ends January 31, and a payment mailed to the county counts on its USPS postmark date.

sections.h2: How can I pay my Gaston County tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online with your Property Key or parcel ID, name or address, by phone at 980-303-2276, by mail or in person.

Mailed payments go to Gaston County Tax Collector, P.O. Box 1578, Gastonia, NC 28053. The county takes checks and money orders by mail and asks you not to mail cash. At 100 E Garrison Boulevard there is a drive-through for cash, check or money order, and inside you can use a credit or debit card with a 2.2% fee. Drop boxes are at both tax office locations, 128 W Main Ave and 100 E Garrison Blvd. Credit card payments by web or phone carry a nominal fee and post within 48 hours. For prepayment plans call 704-866-3030 or 704-866-3037.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Gaston County property value?
sections.html:
File a separate form for each parcel with the County Tax Office, signed by the owner or an authorized representative, before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns.

The board typically adjourns in the last week of April, and the county advertises exact dates in the Gaston Gazette in March. The 2025 board met from April 7 to April 25. If you get a Notice of Value Change you have the later of the adjournment date or 30 days from the notice date. Personal property can be appealed within 30 days of the bill. The board is a panel of five sworn officials chosen by the commissioners, hears the case and rules within 30 days, and its decision letter explains how to go to the Property Tax Commission. North Carolina presumes the assessor's value is correct, so you must show the value substantially exceeds market value as of the reappraisal date.

  • Bring appraisals, comparable sales, photos and, for rentals, income and expense statements.
  • Evidence has to relate to January 1 of the most recent reappraisal year.
  • An appeal cannot be based on inability to pay.

sections.h2: When is the next reappraisal in Gaston County?
sections.html:
The next countywide reappraisal is scheduled for 2027. Gaston has used a four-year cycle, with the last two reappraisals effective January 1, 2019 and January 1, 2023.

State law requires every county to reappraise at least once in eight years, so a four-year cycle is the county's choice. During a reappraisal year the county runs an informal review first. You can use the online form, schedule an appointment with an appraiser or return the form that comes with the reappraisal notice. A decision letter follows, and the value can rise, fall or stay the same. If you still disagree, you have 30 days from mailing of that letter, or until adjournment, to file with the board. Sellers listing in 2027 should read the notice carefully, because a new value changes what a buyer expects the tax to be.

sections.h2: What property tax relief can a Gaston County homeowner get?
sections.html:
Three programs for homeowners apply to a permanent residence, and an owner can receive benefit from only one.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: the greater of $25,000 or 50% of assessed value of the home and up to one acre, for owners 65 or older or totally and permanently disabled who meet the income limit.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: up to $45,000 of assessed value, with no age or income requirement and a form certified through the veterans office.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4% of income for lower incomes and 5% for the next bracket, with a five-year ownership requirement and a new application each year.

The county's filing period runs from January 1 to June 1, and late applications go to the Board of Equalization and Review. The county prints its own income thresholds, and they adjust yearly, so ask the Tax Office on option 6 for the current limit. Present use value for farm and forest land needs 10 acres of agriculture, 5 of horticulture or 20 of forestry, and applications are due in January.

sections.h2: What happens to my tax relief and unpaid tax when I sell in Gaston County?
sections.html:
A sale ends your personal relief and can start a bill for deferred tax. If a residence is sold or the owner dies between January 1 and July 1, the elderly or disabled exclusion is removed for that year, and after July 1 it stays for the current year and drops off the next January 1.

With the circuit breaker, a transfer is a disqualifying event, and the last three years of deferred tax become due with interest. For present use value land, leaving the program bills the difference for the current year plus three prior years with interest, and a new owner has 60 days to file a continued use application. Unpaid tax is a lien on the parcel, so a title company will want the bill paid at closing. Our Gaston County Register of Deeds guide shows where the deed is filed once the tax is settled.

faqs.q: What is the Gaston County property tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The county rate printed on the 2026 chart is 0.5990, and you add your city or fire district rate, such as 0.4700 for Gastonia or 0.1150 for most fire districts. Ask the Tax Office which district your parcel is in.

faqs.q: When do Gaston County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: They become delinquent on January 6. Bills are due September 1, and 2% interest starts January 6 followed by three-quarters of one percent monthly.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Gaston County assessment?
faqs.a: Send the real property appeal form to the County Tax Office before the Board of Equalization and Review adjourns, typically in the last week of April. A Notice of Value Change gives you the later of adjournment or 30 days.

faqs.q: Can I pay Gaston County property tax by phone?
faqs.a: Yes. Call 980-303-2276 and have your property key number from the top right corner of the tax bill. A nominal card fee applies.

faqs.q: When is the next Gaston County reappraisal?
faqs.a: The county's next countywide reappraisal is scheduled for 2027, after reappraisals effective January 1, 2019 and January 1, 2023.
